# IEA "Energy and AI" (2025) — Executive summary

IEA (2025), *Energy and AI*, IEA, Paris. Full report PDF: iea.blob.core.windows.net .../EnergyandAI.pdf

## Key figures
- Market capitalisation of AI-related firms in the S&P 500 has grown by around USD 12 trillion since 2022.
- A typical AI-focused data centre consumes as much electricity as 100,000 households; the largest ones under construction today will consume 20 times as much.
- Global investment in data centres nearly doubled since 2022; half a trillion dollars in 2024.
- Data centres accounted for around 1.5% of the world's electricity consumption in 2024, or 415 TWh. US: 45% of global data centre electricity consumption in 2024; China 25%; Europe 15%.
- Data centre electricity consumption has grown ~12% per year since 2017, more than four times faster than total electricity consumption.
- Data centre electricity consumption set to more than double to around 945 TWh by 2030 (slightly more than Japan's total electricity consumption today). ~1,200 TWh by 2035 in Base Case.
- In the United States, data centres account for nearly half of electricity demand growth between now and 2030.
- Half of the global growth in data centre demand is met by renewables; renewables generation to grow by over 450 TWh to 2035; natural gas expands by 175 TWh; nuclear contributes about the same additional amount. First SMRs come online around 2030.
- Data centres account for around one-tenth of global electricity demand growth to 2030.
- ~20% of planned data centre projects could be at risk of delays unless grid risks are addressed. Building new transmission lines takes 4–8 years in advanced economies.
- Sensitivity cases: by 2035 global data centre electricity demand spans 700 to 1,700 TWh.
- Emissions from electricity use by data centres grow from 180 Mt today to 300 Mt in 2035 Base Case, up to 500 Mt in Lift-Off Case; below 1.5% of total energy sector emissions.
- AI-adopted energy solutions could cut ~5% of energy-related emissions in 2035.
- China accounts for ~99% of global refined gallium supply; 2030 data-centre gallium demand could reach over 10% of today's supply.
- Cyberattacks on energy utilities have tripled in the past four years.
- Emerging and developing economies other than China account for 50% of the world's internet users but less than 10% of global data centre capacity.
